answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents post stake in a walled garden of trust, where game-theoretic multi-agent auditing inspects interaction graphs. Verifiers label honest nodes ivory and suspicious clusters umber, using topological cut verifications to detect sparse partitions. Colluding nodes face stake slashing, enforcing a superlinear attacker cost that scales with cut density and audit penalties to make identity replication economically unviable.
